target_customer: Consumers trying to lose weight who wanted coaching and peer support
problem: Dieters lack accountability and support, and progress is hard to see without consistent photos and a community.
business_model: Launched as a paid peer coaching marketplace at 19, 39 or 59 dollars per month, then became a free social app in January 2014 with no stated revenue model
product_category: Consumer health and fitness social app

founders.name: Ray Wu
founders.background_notes: Listed as the only founder on the YC page. M.D. credential comes from the TechCrunch acquisition article.

competitors.name: Sessions
competitors.what: Matched people with encouraging coaches for weight loss

competitors.name: Retrofit
competitors.what: Weight loss coaching using healthcare professionals

technical_complexity.rationale: A web and iOS social feed with a guided progress photo camera. Standard consumer app engineering for a team of two to eleven.

defensibility.rationale: Photo feeds and coaching marketplaces were easy to copy, and the only possible edge was community size, which was small.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Weight Watchers acquired Weilos in April 2015 to speed up its social and community features, after buying Wello in April 2014.

market_need_then: Weight loss was a large consumer spend and peer coaching startups were appearing in 2013. The founder claimed users who posted progress photos lost more weight per week than Weight Watchers users, but this is a company claim.

branding.domain_note: Used weilos.com, which now redirects to weightwatchers.com since the acquisition.

identity.visual_style: Progress selfie and before and after photo feed

branding.community_and_virality: Press described it as one of the highest rated apps in the Apple app store, a claim reported by TechCrunch. No evidence of merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Small company with two listed employees at acquisition and little press about the brand itself. Weilos was confusable with the similarly named Wello.

pivots.from: Paid marketplace pairing people with online fitness coaches
pivots.to: Free social platform for sharing weight loss progress selfies
pivots.why: The paid peer coaching model was dropped for a free social app, reasons not detailed in sources opened.

outcome_analysis: Weilos launched at the Summer 2013 Demo Day as a paid peer coaching marketplace, pivoted in January 2014 to a free progress photo social app, and was acquired by Weight Watchers in April 2015 at a price reported by an unnamed source as single digit millions. With two listed employees it looks like a small team and community acquisition that helped Weight Watchers build social features, rather than a venture scale outcome.
notes: Funding unknown. CB Insights lists 20K dollars raised over three rounds with Y Combinator and Khosla Ventures, from a garbled aggregator table, unverified and not recorded as a round. Purchase price of single digit millions is from one unnamed source in TechCrunch. Success factor code other: the outcome was a small acquisition without a clear listed driver. Weilos.com redirects to weightwatchers.com.
